title: The pH Scale
summary: From 0 to 14: measuring how acidic or basic something is, universal indicator, dilution, and why each step is 10 times bigger.

ib.note: Logarithmic nature of pH extended in MYP 5 / DP

cbse.chapter: Ch 2: Acids, Bases and Salts (pH scale, importance of pH in everyday life)

objectives: I can describe the pH scale and place common substances on it.
I can use universal indicator colours to estimate pH.
I can explain that each pH unit is a 10× change in acidity.
I can explain the importance of pH in the body, soil and teeth.
misconceptions: pH 2 is only a little more acidic than pH 3 (it's 10× more).
Adding water to an acid can make it basic.
A higher pH number means more acid.
